cards.title: Six new dashes
cards.text: Every dash, lunge, charge and pounce, heroes and enemies, now uses one of six new moves. Mark any that's off.
cards.why: You didn't like how dash slashes worked, from the wolf to the heroes. Each move now has a warning, a body that leans and stretches, a cut drawn where the blade really went, and hits only on what it passes through.

parts.title: Draw cut
parts.text: Settles with the blade at the hip, bursts down a line with the blade swept out, stops past them; each foe crossed gets a thin line and the cut opens a beat later. Iaido; with a spear, Spear Lunge, Spear of the Sky, Bayonet, and spear enemies.

parts.title: Blink chain
parts.text: Sinks, then blinks from foe to foe, crossing each at a slant with a cut and leaving a copy of herself at each stop. The Shade's Shadow Walk.

parts.title: Hook
parts.text: A banked run round the target's side, arriving behind it with the cut across its back. Backstab, the Werewolf's man-form pounce, Sacrifice; bats, succubi, bees, wasps.

parts.title: Feint
parts.text: A hop one way while a copy carries on, a planted foot, then the real dash back across the other flank. The Twinfang's Dash, Crescent Cut; goblins, knife bandits, crabs.

parts.title: Drag and fling
parts.text: Rocks back, runs slow then flat out, picks the first foe up on its front, shoulders the rest aside and flings it (into a wall if there is one). Charge, Shield Rush, Thunder Blow, Shield Bash; orcs and every major's charge.

parts.title: Pounce
parts.text: A flat crouch with a wriggle, a leap that hangs, a landing that rakes three claw lines through what's under it. Wolves, the Alpha, rats, hunter spiders, jackals; Bear Claws and the Werewolf's wolf pounce.

parts.title: Strength
parts.text: Each ability kept within about 10% of its old worth, except where the old one hit nothing (the Twinfang's Dash and Spear of the Sky now deal a little; Iaido III's cut-back now lands). All 26 enemy kinds that changed stay within 10% of their worth per cost.

cards.title: Small foes' dashes cut
cards.text: Rats, goblins and the like dashed without hitting. Now the dash ends in a small cut or pounce.
cards.why: A dash that does nothing reads as broken. It bends an older call that rats dash the way they're moving: the rat's is now a small pounce at whoever it's after. Their worth stays within 10%.

cards.title: Iaido III's cut back
cards.text: Iaido III's cut back used to miss (the first cut knocked them off the line). Now it lands. How hard?
cards.why: Landing at 0.3 of the first cut makes Iaido III about a quarter stronger than before.

options.label: Full
options.text: As hard as the first cut: a big tier III jump.

options.label: A nick
options.text: Barely anything, so tier III is about what it was.

cards.title: Majors carry heroes
cards.text: Majors' charges (and the Herald's and Archon's) now pick up the first light hero and throw it.
cards.why: It reads clearly and fits a big charge, but it's harder on that hero than before, and elite and major moves weren't measured.
cards.pick: Keep it, and I'll measure majors next.

cards.title: Hitting a dashing foe
cards.text: Enemies can now be hit mid-dash; heroes stay untouchable during the dashes that were untouchable before.
cards.why: A charging orc you can't hit felt unfair. Heroes' untouchable dashes (Shadow Walk and the like) are part of those abilities.
